cards.text: Just then a man walks up to Jesus with the biggest question a person can ask: “Teacher, what good thing must I do to obtain eternal life?” No hello, no small talk, straight to ETERNITY.
Jesus catches that word "good" and hands it right back to him: “Why do you ask Me about what is good?” Friend, the man came for a quick answer and got a question back. I KNOW that feeling.

cards.question: Jesus asks the man why he's asking about what is good. What does Jesus say next about who is good?

answers.text: There is only One who is good
Anyone who keeps the Law is good

cards.question: Jesus tells the man that if he wants to enter life, he should keep the ___.

cards.text: The man wants specifics: “Which ones?” It's like your boss says "just follow the rules" and you're staring at a binder thicker than an oven door.
Jesus gives him a list: don't murder, don't commit adultery, don't steal, don't bear false witness, and honor your father and mother. Every one so far is about how you treat people.

cards.question: Jesus' list of commandments for the man is all about how to treat people. What is the last one on the list?
After hearing Jesus' list, the young man says he has kept all of these commandments.
The young man says he has kept every commandment on Jesus' list. What does he ask Jesus next?

cards.text: Jesus tells him: if you want to be perfect, go, sell your possessions and give to the poor. Friend, that's not one more box to check. That's handing over the WHOLE clipboard.

cards.question: If the young man sells his possessions and gives to the poor, what does Jesus say he will have?
After the young man sells everything and gives to the poor, what does Jesus tell him to do then?
When the young man hears what Jesus tells him to do, he goes away in ___.
Jesus told the young man to sell his possessions. Why does the young man go away in sorrow?

cards.text: Then Jesus turns to His disciples. “Truly I tell you, it is hard for a rich man to enter the kingdom of heaven.”

cards.question: Jesus gives a picture of how hard it is for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God. What does He say would have an easier time passing through the eye of a needle?

cards.text: A CAMEL, through the eye of a NEEDLE. Friend, it takes me five tries to get a THREAD through one, and I've got a mustache for hands.

cards.question: When the disciples hear Jesus talk about the camel and the eye of a needle, they shrug it off as no big deal.
The disciples are greatly astonished at what Jesus says about the rich. What do they ask Him?

answers.text: Is it wrong to have wealth

cards.text: Jesus looks right at them. He tells them that with man, this is impossible.

cards.question: Jesus tells His astonished disciples that with man this is impossible. What does He say about God?

answers.text: With God all things are possible
With God the rich must give more
With God only the poor get in

cards.text: Then Peter, one of Jesus' disciples, speaks up: “Look,” “we have left everything to follow You. What then will there be for us?” Peter just said the quiet part OUT LOUD, and honestly? I respect it.

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples that in the renewal of all things, when the Son of Man sits on His glorious throne, those who followed Him will sit on twelve thrones. What will they do there?

answers.text: Judge the twelve tribes of Israel
Rule over the nations of the earth
Guard the gates of the holy city

cards.text: Everyone who has left houses or family or fields for the sake of Jesus' name will receive a hundredfold. Friend, that's walking away from one cookie box and getting handed a HUNDRED.

cards.question: Everyone who leaves things behind for the sake of Jesus' name will receive a hundredfold and will inherit ___ life.
Jesus ends with a flip. He says many who are first will be last. What does He say about the last?

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 5 quotes "just follow the rules", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: "the man came for a quick answer" states as fact why the man came and what he wanted. Matthew 19:16-17 says only that he came up and asked. The text never says he wanted a quick answer.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the quote sentence, "Friend, the man came for a quick answer and got a question back." and "I KNOW that feeling." Only the opening card can have up to 3.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 6 says every commandment so far is about how you treat people, and card 7's question repeats that the list is all about how to treat people. That rules out both wrong answers, "Remember the Sabbath day" and "Do not make any idols," because neither is about treating people. Only the right answer fits.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the paraphrase of Jesus' words, "Friend, that's not one more box to check." and "That's handing over the WHOLE clipboard."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The clipboard joke doesn't click. The core action is selling possessions and giving to the poor. "Handing over the WHOLE clipboard" mixes the box-checking picture of keeping commandments with giving up possessions, and it isn't clear what the clipboard stands for.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: "After the young man sells everything and gives to the poor" reads as if he actually did it. Matthew 19:22 shows that he went away in sorrow and didn't. Card 11 correctly says "If." It also turns "possessions" into "everything."

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The card only reacts to the camel answer from card 2. It tells no new part of the passage and doesn't move it forward. The joke should ride along on a card that carries a moment of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This story card has more than two sentences: the narration with the quote, which holds two sentences of Peter's words, then "Peter just said the quiet part OUT LOUD, and honestly?" and "I respect it."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Peter's words are split into two quoted pieces with nothing between them: "Look," "we have left everything..." The BSB's "Peter replied" has been dropped. Each piece is exact BSB wording, but together they read like two separate lines, and the second starts with a lowercase "we."
findings.question: When a BSB quote is interrupted by a speaker tag, can Papa Dorin drop the tag and place the quoted pieces side by side? Or must he keep the tag, or quote only one piece?

findings.problem: "Jesus ends with a flip" tells the baker the line reverses. That rules out "They will stay last" and "They will be forgotten," so the answer is given away.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Matthew 20:1 opens with "For the kingdom of heaven is like..." and continues Jesus' teaching from 19:30, ending with the same first-and-last line in 20:16. papa-dorin.md ("The story isn't over") says that when a passage's teaching continues in the next passage, he says so at the end. prep-walkthrough.md requires that line only for passages in a story group, and this passage has none. Card 12 also says "Jesus ends with," which may be inaccurate if the teaching goes on.
findings.question: For a passage with no story group whose teaching clearly continues in the next passage, should Prep end with a line saying the teaching isn't done? Should "Jesus ends with" be avoided?
